hook: A rule that sets a highest legal price causes shortages in a market with many sellers. Put the same kind of rule on a single power company and it can do the opposite: more electricity sold, at a lower price. The effect of a policy depends on the market it lands in.

options: ATC that falls over the whole range of demand
ATC that rises over the range of demand
prereq.why: Economies of scale throughout make one firm the cheapest producer.

prereq.q: In a monopsony, a minimum wage between the monopsony wage and the competitive wage
prereq.why: It makes MFC flat at the minimum wage up to labor supply.

prereq.q: A lump-sum tax on a firm changes
options: its ATC but not its MC
its MC but not its ATC
prereq.why: It is fixed whatever the output.

figure.caption: Unregulated, a natural monopoly makes QM and charges PM. The fair-return price PF = ATC gives a normal profit; the socially optimal price PS = MC gives the efficient quantity but a loss.

chain.cause: A monopoly sells more only by cutting its price on every unit
chain.effect: MR is below price, so it restricts output and P > MC

chain.cause: A price ceiling is set where demand meets MC
chain.effect: each unit up to demand earns the ceiling price, so MR equals the ceiling

chain.cause: The firm produces where MC meets that flat MR
chain.effect: output rises toward the efficient quantity and price falls

chain.cause: For a natural monopoly, ATC is above MC at that point
chain.effect: the firm makes a loss, so the regulator subsidizes it or uses the fair-return price P = ATC

ideas: A price ceiling lowers quantity in a competitive market but can raise it for a monopoly, set between the monopoly price and the price where demand meets MC.
Natural monopoly regulation: the socially optimal price (P = MC) is efficient but leaves a loss; the fair-return price (P = ATC) gives a normal profit and less deadweight loss than no regulation.
Lump-sum taxes and subsidies change profit only. Per-unit ones change MC: a tax cuts a monopoly's output and raises its price; a subsidy does the opposite.
A minimum wage lowers employment in a competitive labor market but can raise it in a monopsony.

misconception.wrong: A price ceiling always causes a shortage and lowers the quantity sold.
misconception.right: That is true in a competitive market. For a monopoly, a ceiling below the monopoly price but at or above the price where demand meets MC removes the reason to restrict output, so the firm sells more at the lower price.

summary: The same policy can have different effects in different market structures. A price ceiling cuts output in a competitive market but can raise a monopoly's output by making its marginal revenue flat. Regulators of a natural monopoly choose between the socially optimal price (P = MC, efficient but with a loss that needs a subsidy) and the fair-return price (P = ATC, a normal profit). Lump-sum taxes and subsidies change only profit; per-unit ones change marginal cost and so output and price. A minimum wage lowers employment in a competitive labor market but can raise it in a monopsony.
